title: Have you heard about the Day that covers everything?
subtitle: A question meant to wake up a careless listener
then: Revealed when the Prophet ﷺ had begun preaching openly and the people of Makkah were {trap}hearing it and ignoring it carelessly.{/trap} Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said Al-Ghashiyah is a name of the Day of Judgement, because {idea}it will overwhelm people.{/idea}
now: You have heard about the Day since childhood. It sits in the background like a fire drill notice on the office wall. {idea}The question is personal:{/idea} has it actually reached you, enough to change one thing today?
old: I know about the Day of Judgement. Nothing new there.
new: Knowing about it is not the same as letting it reach me.
try: Read this verse slowly once and answer the question honestly in your head.

title: Some faces that Day will be lowered.
subtitle: Humility that comes too late to help
then: Qatadah said these faces will be {trap}humiliated.{/trap} Ibn Abbas added: {trap}they will be humble, but it will not benefit them.{/trap} The surah begins its picture of that Day with faces, the part of a person that shows everything.
now: The argument you refuse to apologise for. The colleague you will not admit was right. Pride feels strong today. {reward}Humility now is a choice that counts.{/reward} The same humility later is only a result.
old: I will soften when I really have to.
new: Humility is worth something only while I still choose it.
try: Apologise today for one thing you know you got wrong, however small.

title: Working hard, worn out, and still at a loss.
subtitle: Effort spent in the wrong direction
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}they did many deeds and grew weary in them{/trap}, yet ended in the Fire. Ikrimah said: laboring in this life with disobedience. Umar ibn al-Khattab once wept when this verse came to his mind.
now: Seventy-hour weeks. A side hustle. Always tired, always busy, proud of it. {trap}Exhaustion is not proof of worth.{/trap} {idea}The question is who the effort is for, and whether it is right.{/idea}
old: If I am working this hard, I must be doing well.
new: Hard work only counts if it is going the right way.
try: Pick one thing you are tiring yourself out for and ask: does Allah want this from me?

title: They enter a Fire of intense heat.
subtitle: Where the weary, wrong-way effort ends

row.title: to turn me while I can

then: Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the Fire here is {trap}hot with intense heat.{/trap} The verse is brief and plain. The people of Makkah were being shown where heedlessness ends, while there was still time.
now: A warning light on your car dashboard is not cruel. It is the only reason you pull over before the engine is gone. {idea}This verse is that light.{/idea} It asks you to check your direction today.
old: Verses about the Fire are just there to frighten people.
new: The warning is a kindness. It comes while I can still turn back.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you from the Fire, then name one deed you want to change.

title: The only drink is a boiling spring.
subtitle: Thirst with nothing to relieve it
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and As-Suddi said its {trap}heat has reached its limit.{/trap} A spring meant rest and life in the desert. Here it is turned around. Later the surah describes {reward}a flowing spring{/reward} for the other group.
now: Think of the cold water you drink after a long, hot day without a second thought. {idea}Every relief you have today is a gift.{/idea} The verse shows a place where relief is gone, so you notice where it comes from.
old: Water, rest and relief are just normal. I am owed them.
new: Every drink that refreshes me is a mercy I did not earn.
try: Next time you drink water, say Alhamdulillah after it, slowly, and mean it.

title: No food except a bitter thorny plant.
subtitle: The Dari, a plant the Arabs knew well
then: Mujahid and Qatadah said Dari is a plant called {trap}Ash-Shibriq, which the people of the Hijaz call Dari when it dries, and it is poisonous.{/trap} The listeners knew it as something no animal would choose to eat.
now: Your fridge is full. You open it and complain there is nothing to eat. {idea}The verse makes you stop and see how much you have.{/idea} It also reminds you that what you eat there depends on what you do here.
old: Having food is normal. Complaining about it is harmless.
new: Food is a gift here. What I am given there depends on my deeds.
try: Share one meal or snack with someone today, and eat your own with gratitude.

title: It neither nourishes nor stops the hunger.
subtitle: Food that does not do what food is for
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}the intent in eating it will not be achieved, and nothing harmful is repelled by it.{/trap} The section on the people of the Fire ends here, before the surah turns to the joyful faces.
now: An hour of scrolling and you feel emptier. Another order online, and the lift lasts until it arrives. {trap}Some things you keep eating never feed you.{/trap} {idea}Notice them now, while there is still real food on offer.{/idea}
old: If I keep consuming, eventually I will feel full.
new: Some things never feed me. I can turn to what does.
try: Notice one habit you reach for that leaves you emptier, and skip it once today.

title: Other faces that Day will glow with joy.
subtitle: The surah turns to the people of Paradise
then: After the wretched, Allah turns to the happy. Ibn Kathir: {reward}pleasure will be noticeable in their faces{/reward}, and {idea}this will only occur due to their striving.{/idea} The same Day, two very different faces.
now: You know the face of a nurse finishing a hard shift she is proud of, or a parent at a child's graduation. {reward}Joy that grew from effort.{/reward} The verse says that kind of face is waiting for those who strive now.
old: Some people are just blessed. I am not one of them.
new: Joy on that Day grows from striving I can begin now.
try: Do one act of worship today and picture your face glad on the Day for it.

title: Pleased with what their effort became.
subtitle: Looking back at your deeds and being glad
then: Sufyan explained: {reward}they will be pleased with their deeds.{/reward} The contrast is sharp. Verse 3 showed people {trap}worn out by their labor{/trap}. Here people also worked, and are glad they did.
now: You will be tired either way. Tired from overtime that disappears, or tired from fasting, caring for a parent, waking for Fajr. {reward}Only one kind of tired leaves you glad looking back.{/reward}
old: Any effort for the next life just feels like extra strain.
new: Effort for Allah is the one tiredness I will be glad about.
try: Tonight, recall one good deed from today and thank Allah for letting you do it.

title: In a garden lifted high.
subtitle: An elevated Paradise, secure and bright
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}elevated and brilliant, secure in their dwellings.{/reward} For listeners who lived in flat desert valleys, a high, green garden was a picture of everything good.
now: You scroll property listings late at night. The penthouse, the view, the safe area. {idea}The longing for a high, safe home is real.{/idea} The verse points it at a home that will not need a mortgage or a lock.
old: My dream home is the best thing I can work toward.
new: My longing for a safe, high home is a hint of the garden.
try: Next time you daydream about a better home, ask Allah for a home in the lofty garden.

title: Not one foolish or hurtful word is heard there.
subtitle: Paradise is free of harmful, empty speech
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}they will not hear any foolish word.{/reward} He ties it to other verses where Paradise has no idle talk or sin, {reward}only the saying: Salam, Salam.{/reward}
now: The comments section. The tense family group chat. The office gossip in the kitchen. {trap}So much of what hurts you arrives as words.{/trap} {idea}A place with none of that is part of the reward.{/idea}
old: Harsh talk is just part of life. I barely notice it.
new: A life free of hurtful words is a gift, and I can start it in my own speech.
try: Go one conversation today without a single sarcastic or hurtful word.

title: Springs that keep flowing.
subtitle: Running water that never runs out
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {reward}flowing springs{/reward}, not just one. He records the hadith that {reward}the rivers of Paradise spring from beneath hills of musk.{/reward} In a desert land, running water was the clearest sign of life.
now: A dry summer. A water shortage on the news. A bottle bought at a station for too much money. {reward}Water that never stops, never costs, never runs dry{/reward} is the picture the verse paints.
old: Water is just there. I never think about it.
new: Every flowing tap is a small sign of the springs that never stop.
try: Offer someone a glass of water today, and remember those who lack clean water in your dua.

title: Couches raised high to rest on.
subtitle: Rest and honor for those who strove
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}lofty, delightful, numerous couches, with elevated ceilings.{/reward} He mentions that scholars said these thrones lower themselves when the friend of Allah wishes to sit. After the striving of verse 9 comes rest.
now: You stand all day at the counter, on the ward, in the classroom. You come home and drop onto the sofa. {idea}That relief is a small taste.{/idea} {reward}A raised seat of honor waits after the work of this life.{/reward}
old: Rest is something I steal between duties.
new: Real, honored rest is promised after the striving.
try: Take five minutes of rest today and use them to thank Allah for strength to work.

title: Cups already set out, ready for you.
subtitle: Nothing to wait for, nothing to fetch
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}drinking containers that are prepared and presented{/reward} for whoever of the people of Paradise wants them. No searching, no asking. The verse is short, like a host's table already laid.
now: The parent who is always last to sit down at dinner. The worker who refills everyone's mug and never their own. {reward}There, it is all set out for you.{/reward} Your quiet serving here is not unseen.
old: I always serve others and no one notices.
new: Allah sees the serving, and has a table set for me.
try: Make tea or bring water for someone today, quietly, with this verse in mind.

title: Cushions lined up in neat rows.
subtitle: Comfort arranged with care
then: Ibn Abbas said {reward}An-Namariq are pillows{/reward}, and Ikrimah, Qatadah and others agreed. The detail is homely: cushions lined up, as when a family prepares the room for guests they love.
now: You remember arriving at a relative's house and seeing the guest room made up for you: fresh pillows, everything in order. {reward}That feeling of being expected{/reward} is what the verse holds out.
old: Paradise feels vague and far from my real life.
new: It is described in the details of a home made ready for me.
try: Prepare a small comfort for a guest or family member today, with care.

title: Carpets spread out everywhere you want to sit.
subtitle: The last detail of the garden's comfort
then: Ibn Abbas said {reward}Az-Zarabi are carpets.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains that spread out means {reward}placed here and there for whoever would like to sit.{/reward} With this, the picture of the joyful faces is complete.
now: Your feet on a cold tiled floor at Fajr. The worn mat you pray on. {idea}Each small comfort here is a hint, not the real thing.{/idea} The real one is spread out, waiting, wherever you choose to sit.
old: I want comfort now, not promised comfort later.
new: Comfort here is a taste. Lasting comfort is spread out for those who strive.
try: Pray one prayer today slowly on your mat, and ask Allah for the carpets of the garden.

title: Look at the camel. How was it made?
subtitle: The animal their whole life depended on

row.title: an amazing creation
sub: look at how it was made

then: The people of Makkah were {trap}ignoring the message carelessly.{/trap} So the surah points at the camel, their most common animal. Ibn Kathir: {idea}extremely strong, yet gentle, led by a weak rider{/idea}, and giving milk, meat and hair.
now: Your phone, your cat on the sofa, your own hand. You use them so often you stopped seeing them. {idea}The verse asks you to look again at the most ordinary thing in your day.{/idea}
old: Everyday things are boring. Signs must be something dramatic.
new: The most ordinary thing in my life is a sign if I look.
try: Pick one animal or object you see daily and spend one minute noticing how it is made.

title: And the sky: how was it raised?
subtitle: The roof over every journey
then: The judge Shurayh used to say: {idea}come out with us to look at the camels and how they were created, and at the sky and how it was raised.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We built it?
now: You check the sky only on a weather app. Head down on the commute, eyes on the screen. {idea}The sky has been held up over you your whole life{/idea} and you have barely looked at it this week.
old: The sky is just there. It does not say anything to me.
new: The raised sky is a daily sign of the One who raised it.
try: Step outside today, look up for one full minute, and say SubhanAllah.

title: And the mountains: how were they set firm?
subtitle: Mountains planted so the earth stays steady
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}they are firmly fixed so that the earth does not sway with its dwellers{/idea}, and He made them with benefits and minerals. The traveler in Arabia always had a mountain in front of him. The verse asks him to think about who put it there.
now: The ground under your house is still while you sleep. You never think about it until the news shows an earthquake somewhere. {idea}Your steadiness was arranged long before you needed it.{/idea}
old: Stability in my life is mostly my own doing.
new: Even the ground I stand on was made steady for me.
try: When you feel shaken today, place your feet flat on the floor and remember who keeps it still.

title: And the earth: how was it spread out?
subtitle: Four things the traveler sees, one Maker

row.title: He made it, so He is my Lord

then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}He directs the bedouin to consider what he himself witnesses{/idea}: the camel he rides, the sky above, the mountain ahead, the earth beneath. A bedouin named Dimam later swore by these same things when he asked the Prophet ﷺ if Allah had sent him.
now: Your morning walk to the bus stop. Pavement under you, sky above, a hill or a skyline ahead. {idea}Four signs on the most boring route of your day.{/idea} They all ask the same question: who made this, and do you live like you know?
old: I believe Allah made everything, but it does not change my day.
new: If He made all I see, He is the One I should be living for.
try: On your next walk, name the four things this passage mentions and say who made them.

title: So remind. Reminding is your whole job.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ is told his role is to remind
then: After the signs, the instruction: {idea}remind the people with what you have been sent with.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {idea}your duty is only to convey, and on Us is the reckoning.{/idea}
now: You keep telling your brother to pray and he keeps not praying. You start to feel you have failed. {idea}Your job was to remind, kindly and clearly.{/idea} The rest is not in your hands.
old: If they do not change, my reminding was a failure.
new: My part is the reminder. The result belongs to Allah.
try: Make dua for someone you have been trying to remind, and let go of the outcome.

title: You are not their controller.
subtitle: No one can force faith into a heart
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: {idea}you are not a dictator over them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: {trap}you cannot create faith in their hearts.{/trap} Ibn Zayd said: you are not the one who can force them to believe.
now: The nagging messages. The pressure at family gatherings. Turning a teenager's every mistake into a sermon. {trap}Control often pushes people further away.{/trap} {idea}Faith is placed in a heart by Allah, not by force.{/idea}
old: If I push hard enough, I can make them believe.
new: I cannot control a heart. I can only remind and pray.
try: Replace one lecture you planned to give someone this week with one kind act toward them.

title: But the one who turns his back and rejects.
subtitle: Turning away from the truth by heart and tongue
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}he turns away from acting on its pillars, and disbelieves in the truth with his heart and his tongue.{/trap} He compares it to the verse: he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away.
now: It rarely starts with a big rejection. You skip, then you avoid, then you argue against what you skipped. {idea}Turning away is a direction, and you can notice it early in yourself.{/idea}
old: Turning away is something other people do.
new: I check which part of the truth I am quietly turning my back on.
try: Name one thing you know is right but have been avoiding, and take one step toward it.

title: Allah Himself will deal with him.
subtitle: The greatest punishment, decided by Allah alone
then: The verse is plain: {trap}Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.{/trap} Coming right after you are not their controller, it puts the judgement where it belongs: {idea}with Allah, not with the one reminding.{/idea}
now: It is easy to sit in judgement of people online, deciding who is doomed. {idea}The verse takes that seat away from you.{/idea} Judgement is Allah's. Your own record is the one you can still work on.
old: I can tell who is going to be punished.
new: Punishment is Allah's to decide. My task is my own record.
try: When you catch yourself judging someone today, turn the thought into a dua for both of you.

title: Every one of them is coming back to Us.
subtitle: The return is to Allah, without exception

row.title: a return
sub: back to the One who sent you

then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}their place of return and their resort.{/idea} The surah opened by asking about the Overwhelming Day. Near its close it says plainly where everyone is heading.
now: Boarding pass, return flight. You always check the return date. {idea}Your life has a return date too{/idea}, and the One you return to is the One who made the camel, the sky, and you.
old: Life goes on and then it just stops.
new: Life is a journey that ends in a return to Allah.
try: Say Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un once today, slowly, about your own life.

title: And then it is on Us to take their account.
subtitle: Every deed reckoned and repaid fairly
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}We will reckon their deeds and requite them.{/idea} {reward}If they did good, they will receive good{/reward}, and if evil, evil. The surah ends here, the account placed with Allah, as it told the Prophet ﷺ in verse 21.
now: The extra shift no one thanked you for. The patience with a difficult parent. The charity you never mentioned. {reward}The account is kept by Allah, and nothing good is dropped.{/reward}
old: Most of what I do goes unnoticed and unrewarded.
new: Every deed is counted by Allah, and good is met with good.
try: Tonight, list three things you did today that you would want in your account.
